title: Overnight Minimum-Flow Baseline Drift
dataSources: Whole-home water flow (`watermeter:flow`), water pressure (`waterpressure:reading`), irrigation control (`irrigation:zone`), water-heater events (`waterheater:event`), greywater tanks (`greywater:tank`), and utility sensors for pumps and softeners (`sumppump:event`, `wellpump:event`, `watersoftener:status`).
app: Water and plumbing telemetry from smart water meters, pressure sensors, irrigation controllers, sump and well pumps, greywater tanks, and water-heater sensors streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and vendor APIs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=watermeter:flow
| where date_hour>=1 AND date_hour<=4
| timechart span=1d min(flow_lpm) as overnight_min_flow_lpm
description: Charts the lowest overnight flow each day so small persistent leaks become visible even before they are constant.
value: Night hours are your cleanest baseline, and rising minimum flow is a strong early warning for creeping plumbing waste.
implementation: Track whole-home flow continuously and compare the quietest overnight periods across days or weeks.
visualization: Line chart of daily overnight minimum flow.
grandmaExplanation: It counts whether your quiet overnight water use is slowly creeping up, which can hint at a hidden leak.
